rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: train_n=200, val_n=6, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, seed=123, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, n_iter=400, outer_wall_s=1200, lr=0.0023, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=7, proj_kernel=7, img_kernel=5, proj_sx=1.0, proj_sy=2.0, proj_sr=0.02, img_sx=1.5, img_sy=1.5, img_sr=0.02, rationale=iter-8: CEILING-CONFIRMATION (seed-invariance) probe. ONE knob changed vs the iter-6 hr-best base (seed 42->123); all 18 other fields held IDENTICAL to demo_dl_dual_domain_bilateral_n2i_iter_06.json (img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 LOOSE demo-correct, n_iter=400). seed is the FIRST not-yet-tried axis -- it was pinned at 42 across iters 1-7, so this is a genuinely new probe (not a re-touch of an exhausted lever). Read iters 5-7 BY HEADROOM (the campaign primary, PSNR/noise-sensitive on demo): iter-5 img_sr->0.02 revert hr 0.3320; iter-6 img_n_bf=7 hr 0.3330 (depth DEAD FLAT vs iter-3 n_bf=5 0.3335); iter-7 n_iter 400->800 hr 0.3346 (per-scan Adam budget DEAD FLAT). BOTH capacity axes are now exhausted: image-domain DEPTH (img_n_bf, hr slope collapsed to ~0 by n_bf=5) AND per-scan OPTIMIZER budget (n_iter, flat at 800 -- and the 6-param bilateral physically CANNOT overfit one scan, so more steps cannot lift hr). img_sr is exhausted+substrate-confirmed wrong-direction (demo wants LOOSE 0.02; tightening to 0.0005 collapsed hr 0.3335->0.1998 at iter-4). proj_n_bf is in the symmetry trap (near-identity proj sigmas -> wasted params). FAILURE MODE being documented: the 6-param bilateral is at its ~hr 0.33 STRUCTURAL ceiling on demo phantoms -- it cannot extract more than the 64-view (half of 128) FBP noise floor allows on this synthetic substrate. The open question this probe closes: is hr~0.333 a STABLE structural bound or an artifact of the single seed=42 val split? Re-running the identical iter-6 config under a fresh seed (123 -> different 6-scene val draw AND different warm-start/per-scan init noise) tests invariance. HYPOTHESIS: hr lands ~0.333 again (within +/-0.01) -> CONFIRMS the ~hr 0.33 ceiling is seed-stable and structural, not a lucky split. If hr instead swings widely, the ceiling is split-sensitive and val_n should be raised next to tighten the estimate. Chose seed over (a) img_n_bf/n_iter (both DEAD FLAT, exhausted), (b) img_sr (exhausted, wrong-direction), (c) proj_n_bf (symmetry trap), (d) lr/grad_clip/warm_start (also untried, but seed-invariance is the canonical first ceiling-confirmation probe and was explicitly named as the next step in the iter-6/iter-7 rationales). Held fixed at iter-6 values: img_n_bf=7, img_sr=0.02 (LOOSE, demo-correct), n_iter=400, proj_n_bf=1, kernels (proj_k=7/img_k=5), proj sigmas (1.0/2.0/0.02), img spatial sigmas (img_sx=1.5/img_sy=1.5), lr=2.3e-3, warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, train_n=200, val_n=6, grad_clip=1.0. Wall: iter-6 ran ~828 s at n_iter=400; seed is a pure init/split change with ZERO added compute, so wall ~unchanged, comfortably under the 1800 s sbatch wall and the 1200 s outer_wall_s internal guard (well under the 15-min budget). This iter DOCUMENTS the ~hr 0.33 ceiling toward iter-20. PER-IMAGE bilateral N2I, AGENT4CT_DATASET=phantoms; do NOT revert to amortized.
